physiological_effect.name: Insomnia
physiological_effect.description: A disorder characterized by difficulty in falling asleep and/or remaining asleep. (NCI CTCAE)

physiological_effect.name: Hallucinations
physiological_effect.description: A disorder characterized by a false sensory perception in the absence of an external stimulus. (NCI CTCAE)

physiological_effect.name: Confusion
physiological_effect.description: A disorder characterized by a lack of clear and orderly thought and behavior. (NCI CTCAE)

physiological_effect.name: Fatigue
physiological_effect.description: A disorder characterized by a state of generalized weakness with a pronounced inability to summon sufficient energy to accomplish daily activities. (NCI CTCAE)

physiological_effect.name: Irritability
physiological_effect.description: A disorder characterized by an abnormal responsiveness to stimuli or physiological arousal; may be in response to pain, fright, a drug, an emotional situation or a medical condition. (NCI CTCAE)

physiological_effect.name: Headache
physiological_effect.description: A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in various parts of the head, not confined to the area of distribution of any nerve. (NCI CTCAE)

physiological_effect.name: Nausea
physiological_effect.description: A disorder characterized by a queasy sensation and/or the urge to vomit. (NCI CTCAE)

physiological_effect.name: Delusions
physiological_effect.description: A disorder characterized by false personal beliefs held contrary to reality, despite contradictory evidence and common sense. (NCI CTCAE)

physiological_effect.name: Agitation
physiological_effect.description: A disorder characterized by a state of restlessness associated with unpleasant feelings of irritability and tension. (NCI CTCAE)

physiological_effect.name: Stimulant psychosis
physiological_effect.category: Adverse health effect > Nervous system disorder > Central nervous system disorder > Psychiatric disorder > Psychoactive substance abuse disorder
physiological_effect.description: A psychotic disorder typically cause by an overdose on psychostimulants, resulting in hallucinations, paranoia, and/or delusions.

physiological_effect.name: Psychosis
physiological_effect.category: Adverse health effect > Nervous system disorder > Central nervous system disorder > Psychiatric disorder
physiological_effect.description: A mental disorder characterized by personality change, impaired functioning, and loss of touch with reality. (NCI)

physiological_effect.name: Diarrhea
physiological_effect.description: A disorder characterized by an increase in frequency and/or loose or watery bowel movements. (NCI CTCAE)

process.name: Caffeine Metabolism
process.category: Naturally occurring process > Biological process > Biochemical pathway > Metabolic pathway
process.description: Caffeine is obtained from diet including coffee and other beverages and is absorbed in the stomach and small intestine. In the liver, the cytochrome P450 oxidase enzyme system and specifically CYP1A2 metabolizes caffeine into paraxanthine to increase lipolysis and increase free fatty acids and glycerol levels in the blood, theobromine to dilate blood vessels and increase urine volume and theophylline which relaxes bronchi smooth muscles. In the lysosome, these metabolites undergo further metabolism into methyluric acids before being excreted in the urine.

process.name: Asthma
process.category: Naturally occurring process > Biological process > Biochemical pathway
process.description: A bronchial disease that is characterized by chronic inflammation and narrowing of the airways, which is caused by a combination of environmental and genetic factors. the disease has symptom recurring periods of wheezing (a whistling sound while breathing), has symptom chest tightness, has symptom shortness of breath, has symptom mucus production and has symptom coughing. the symptoms appear due to a variety of triggers such as allergens, irritants, respiratory infections, weather changes, exercise, stress, reflux disease, medications, foods and emotional anxiety. (do).

role.name: Food additive
role.description: A chemical added to food  to preserve or enhance the food qualities

role.name: Drug metabolite
role.description: A chemical which was introduced to the body as a pharmaceutical or narcotic drug, and further biotransformed

role.name: Waste product
role.description: A chemical that is generated in a metabolic process and is destined to be excreted from the body. It commonly consists of water, nitrogenous compounds or carbon dioxide and can be a metabolic byproduct or a degradation product (such as urobilin metabolised from bilirubin which is a degradation product of hemoglobin).

role.name: Pesticide
role.description: A chemical or preparation used to kill or control pests, such as insects, weeds, plant pathogens, rodents, etc. (EPA).

role.name: Tachycardic
role.description: A chemical that causes an abnormal increase in heart rate.

role.name: Pharmaceutical
role.description: A chemical administered as a medicinal drug, aiming to modify a biological process in the body and as a result to alleviate a symptom or treat a health condition.

role.name: Adjuvant
role.category: Industrial application > Manufacturing industry > Material processing agent > Coloring agent > Fluorescent agent
role.description: A chemical used in as pharmacological or immunological agent, that modifies the effect of other agents such as drugs or vaccines while having few if any direct effects when given by itself.

role.name: Drug
role.description: A chemical or preparation that causes a physiological effect in the body upon exposure

role.name: CGMP-phosphodiesterase inhibitor
role.category: Biological role > Modulator > Inhibitor > Enzyme inhibitor
role.description: A chemical that binds to and decreases the activity of cGMP-phosphodiesterase

role.name: CAMP-phosphodiesterase inhibitor
role.category: Biological role > Modulator > Inhibitor > Enzyme inhibitor
role.description: A chemical that binds to and decreases the activity of cAMP-phosphodiesterase

role.name: Phosphodiesterase inhibitor
role.category: Biological role > Modulator > Inhibitor > Enzyme inhibitor
role.description: A chemical that blocks the action of phosphodiesterase

role.name: Diuretic
role.category: Industrial application > Manufacturing industry > Material processing agent > Coloring agent > Fluorescent agent
role.description: A chemical that increases the production of urine.

role.name: Pyrogenic
role.description: An agent that induces fever, by generating heat.

role.name: Analgesic
role.category: Industrial application > Manufacturing industry > Material processing agent > Coloring agent > Fluorescent agent
role.description: A chemical that causes analgesia, relief of pain

role.name: Mutagen
role.description: A chemical substance that alters the genetic material of an organism, and increases the frequency of mutations above the naturally-occuring rate

role.name: Anti carcinogenic
role.description: A substance that inhibits or prevents the proliferation of neoplasms.

role.name: Anti feedant
role.description: Any substance that inhibits normal feeding behaviour. A naturally occurring substance in certain plants that adversely affects insects or other animals that eat them.

role.name: Anti cariogenic
role.description: Any substance introduced into a living organism with therapeutic or diagnostic purpose.

role.name: Anti narcotic
role.description: A sunbstance that blunts the senses, as opium,morphine, belladonna, and alcohol, that in large quantities cause produceeuphoria, stupor, or coma, and when used constantly can causehabituation or addiction. It can be used in medicine to relieve pain, cause sedation, and induce sleep.

role.name: Choleretic
role.description: An agent, or substance, that increases the volume of secretion of bile from the liver as well as the amount of solids secreted.

role.name: Ergotamine enhancer
role.description: An agent that stimulates production of ergotamine, a fungal secondary metabolite that also has biological activity as a vasoconstrictor.

role.name: Analeptic
role.description: A chemical or preparation that directly affects secretion from the thyroid glend

role.name: (+)-inotropic
role.description: An agent that alters the force or energy of muscular contractions. Positively inotropic agents increase the strength of muscular contraction.

role.name: Insecticide
role.description: A chemical used to control insect life harmful to man. (EPA).

role.name: Vasodilator agent
